Explore authentic historical maps connected to Indigenous North America. Follow each map into its archive to examine the original, enlarge the details, and read its catalogue record.

Browse 17 maps ↓Explore today’s region directory ↗
Read the map’s date and maker. These documents include Indigenous knowledge, colonial cartography and government surveys. Their names, classifications and boundaries reflect particular times and purposes. They do not establish present Indigenous territories. A surviving copy is identified as a copy. Date filters follow the catalogue’s publication or copy date; an earlier design is explained in the record.

12 directory entries have reviewed map connections so far. This is a growing selection, including overlapping reading labels.

1836 · Historical scholarship

Map of the Indian tribes of North America, about 1600 A.D. along the Atlantic, & about 1800 A.D. westwardly

Albert Gallatin; American Antiquarian Society

Gallatin assembled this map for an American Antiquarian Society publication in 1836. Its title distinguishes eastern depictions around 1600 from western depictions around 1800. Compare its historical naming and classifications with later maps; its labels do not define current communities or borders.

London, 1777 · Colonial cartography

Canada and neighboring borderlands, 1777

Claude Joseph Sauthier; William Faden

A British colonial map of southern Quebec and neighboring borderlands, compiled from French surveys. Its military and commercial framing offers evidence about colonial priorities and representations of Indigenous people. Read it as a historical viewpoint, without treating it as present territorial authority.

1891 · Federal survey / administration

Linguistic Stocks of American Indians North of Mexico.

John Wesley Powell

Powell grouped North American Indigenous languages into the linguistic stocks used by nineteenth-century federal ethnology. Read this as a historical classification project, including its names and large colored areas, alongside language and community accounts. These areas do not establish present boundaries.

1760 · Colonial engraving / mediated Indigenous geographic knowledge

A new map of the Cherokee Nation

Thomas Kitchin (engraver); unidentified Indigenous draught credited on the sheet

1873 · Federal reservation administration

Proposed Nez Perce reservation in the Wallowa Valley

Office of Indian Affairs, U.S. Department of the Interior (archive attribution; individual drafter unidentified)

This federal map outlines a proposed reservation in northeastern Oregon. Its title explicitly names Nez Perce people and the Wallowa Valley; red lines, rivers and survey divisions explain the proposed tract. Read it alongside the government's 1873 order. The map records an administrative proposal rather than the full Nez Perce homeland or present boundaries.

A growing map room

This selection brings archive records together. Some have a reusable preview; others open at the holding institution. Reviewed connections lead to individual directory profiles, where the same maps appear with an explanation of their relevance. Unlinked records remain under review.

Follow the originals

Original titles can contain outdated language. Archive descriptions and our inspection notes explain what was checked. A linked record is not a completed nation-level research review.
